decision_rule: Treat M105 as a qualified positive smoke only if objective loss improves, normal M62-level behavior is retained, reset and zero-response ablations reduce success, and braking/lateral/yaw hidden-envelope lift are positive on the tested checkpoint.
failure_criteria: outcome loss improves but reset-hidden behavior does not degrade
braking or lateral hidden-envelope lift is negative versus reset hidden
normal behavior regresses versus M62 or M102
the objective introduces hidden physics or oracle labels into actor inputs
hypothesis: M103 failed because fitting reset-sensitive snippets alone changed the closed-loop trajectory distribution enough to lose hidden-envelope retention. A broad action-retention anchor can keep M102's hidden belief while recovering outcome-relevant behavior dependence.
success_criteria: uses only deployable actor observations and training-time outcome labels
preserves M62/M102 normal behavior and clearance margin
reset or zero-response ablations degrade success or clearance
retains positive braking, lateral, and yaw response-hidden-minus-reset envelope lift
records objective repeats and full behavior and hidden-envelope gates
